beats.trigger: What may the agent read? What may it change? What must come back to a human?

beats.trigger: Scope (give the agent less). Split (two agents, different trust levels). Filter (post-process output). Gate (human approves). Review (a second agent judges).
beats.got: Five ways to make it safer. Gate and scope I understand, the others not so much.

beats.trigger: Accept the residual on record, or close the door.
beats.got: Some risk stays, and someone signs for it.

beats.trigger: More context makes a good answer likelier. Less access makes a bad answer smaller.
beats.got: Give the agent less access and the mistakes get smaller.

beats.got: Don't give it write access to the dispatch system. Easy, I know this logic from depot keys.

beats.got: A skill is a saved checklist the agent can reuse. I am not sure what system I built before.

take_homes: Ask three things about any agent: what can it read, what can it change, what must a person approve.
The safest fix is not giving it access in the first place, like write access to dispatch.
The agent can check my system against company rules and make a table, and saying "I can't tell" is ok.

monday.move: nothing, unless my depot managers ask; maybe look at what the reporting agent could read
monday.blocker: no time, and the reporting data is stuck in a system I cannot export from without IT

misconception.why: Everything was about software systems and policy files. The AI-for-customers-only idea did not change, but the idea that access is like keys at a depot made some sense.

one_line: Too much text and too many English words, but the idea of giving the agent less access I understood, and the audit table was something real.
